components.cost_effect: Index evaluation uses stored statistics and no additional reward queries.
components.key_estimate: The source Proof bounds E[T_i(n)] by 8 ln(n)/Delta_i^2 + 1 + pi^2/3 for a suboptimal arm; full performance scope is in thm.P093.regret.
components.name: Empirical mean with count-dependent confidence radius
components.operation: Use S_i/N_i + sqrt(2 ln(n)/N_i) as the selection index.
components.requires: Positive counts from initialization; bounded stationary independent arm rewards for the cited analysis.
transfer_checks: A change to reward support, dependence, stationarity or feedback requires a new concentration and counting argument.

limitations.statement: This record supplies sequential reward collection, not a terminal best-arm identification procedure or guarantee.
The cited performance is for this selected policy; it does not characterize unrestricted Oracle Complexity or justify dependent, nonstationary or unbounded rewards.

performance_links.scope_note: Selected UCB1 expected regret upper bound under the full stated reward assumptions.

variants.cost: Each round costs one selected-arm reward observation, including the K initialization observations. Separately, a direct implementation evaluates K indices and an argmax per post-initialization round, updates one count and sum, and stores O(K) numbers. These arithmetic/storage counts describe the implementation, not an additional source performance theorem; no bit-complexity claim is made.
variants.name: UCB1, Figure 1
variants.output: One selected arm and observed reward each round, forming a sequential action/reward history. No terminal recommendation or identification confidence is supplied.
public_inputs: Integer K>1 and access to each arm; known reward support [0,1].
No means, gaps, reward laws or horizon are needed.
variants.query_and_update: After n completed plays choose j maximizing S_i/N_i + sqrt(2 ln(n)/N_i). Observe the next reward x from arm j. Set S_j<-S_j+x, N_j<-N_j+1 and n<-n+1; other arm statistics remain unchanged. Figure 1 leaves ties unspecified; choosing the least maximizing index is an explicit implementation convention.
variants.requirements: Each arm has an iid reward sequence with support [0,1], unknown law and mean; rewards across arms are independent. Only the selected arm's next reward is observed.
variants.state_and_initialization: Play each arm once. Store its count N_i=1 and observed reward sum S_i; set total completed plays n=K. The initialization order is not specified by the source; increasing arm order is a reproducible implementation convention.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: No tuned parameter. Continue indefinitely or truncate at an externally chosen integer horizon; initialization plays count toward that horizon.

use_restrictions: Tie-breaking and initialization order conventions are explicitly distinguished from the source sketch.
Reference is a staging readiness claim; independent review and publication have not occurred.
